verses.original: ἐν σαββάτῳ δὲ Ἐγένετο αὐτὸν διαπορεύεσθαι διὰ σπορίμων καὶ αὐτοῦ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἔτιλλον τοὺς στάχυας ψώχοντες ταῖς χερσίν καὶ ἤσθιον
verses.transliteration: en sabbatō de Egeneto auton diaporeuesthai dia sporimōn kai autou hoi mathētai etillon tous stachyas psōchontes tais chersin kai ēsthion
verses.literal: - [One] Sabbath - - [Jesus] was passing through [the] grainfields and His - disciples began to pick the heads of grain rub [them] in [their] hands and eat [them]

verses.original: δὲ τινὲς τῶν Φαρισαίων εἶπαν Τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν
verses.transliteration: de tines tōn Pharisaiōn eipan Ti poieite ho ouk exestin tois sabbasin
verses.literal: But some of the Pharisees asked Why are you doing what vvv is unlawful [on] the Sabbath

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς Οὐδὲ ἀνέγνωτε τοῦτο ὃ Δαυὶδ ἐποίησεν ὁπότε αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ ὄντες μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἐπείνασεν
verses.transliteration: Kai ho Iēsous apokritheis eipen pros autous Oude anegnōte touto ho Dauid epoiēsen hopote autos kai hoi ontes met’ autou epeinasen
verses.literal: - - Jesus replied . . . . . . . . . vvv Have you not read vvv what David did when he and his companions . . . . . . . . . were hungry

verses.original: ὡς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως καὶ ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἔφαγεν οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς ἱερεῖς φαγεῖν
verses.transliteration: hōs eisēlthen eis ton oikon tou Theou kai labōn tous artous tēs protheseōs kai edōken tois met’ autou ephagen hous ouk exestin ei mē monous tous hiereis phagein
verses.literal: - He entered . . . the house - of God - took the consecrated bread . . . . . . and gave [it] to his companions . . . . . . [and] ate what - is lawful only for . . . . . . the priests to eat

verses.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐστιν Κύριός τοῦ σαββάτου
verses.transliteration: kai elegen autois ho Huios tou anthrōpou estin Kyrios tou sabbatou
verses.literal: Then [Jesus] declared - The Son - of Man is Lord of the Sabbath

verses.original: ἐν ἑτέρῳ σαββάτῳ δὲ Ἐγένετο αὐτὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν καὶ διδάσκειν καὶ ἄνθρωπος ἦν ἐκεῖ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἡ δεξιὰ ἡ χεὶρ ἦν ξηρά
verses.transliteration: en heterō sabbatō de Egeneto auton eiselthein eis tēn synagōgēn kai didaskein kai anthrōpos ēn ekei kai autou hē dexia hē cheir ēn xēra
verses.literal: On another Sabbath - - [Jesus] entered . . . the synagogue and was teaching and a man was there - [whose] - right - hand was withered

verses.original: ἵνα εὕρωσιν κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ δὲ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι παρετηροῦντο αὐτὸν εἰ θεραπεύει ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ
verses.transliteration: hina heurōsin katēgorein autou de hoi grammateis kai hoi Pharisaioi paretērounto auton ei therapeuei en tō sabbatō
verses.literal: vvv Looking for a reason to accuse [Jesus] - the scribes and - Pharisees were watching Him closely . . . [to see] if He would heal on the Sabbath

verses.original: δὲ Αὐτὸς ᾔδει αὐτῶν τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς δὲ εἶπεν τῷ ἀνδρὶ τῷ ἔχοντι τὴν ξηρὰν χεῖρα Ἔγειρε καὶ στῆθι εἰς τὸ μέσον καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη
verses.transliteration: de Autos ēdei autōn tous dialogismous de eipen tō andri tō echonti tēn xēran cheira Egeire kai stēthi eis to meson kai anastas estē
verses.literal: But [Jesus] knew their - thoughts and said to the man - with the withered hand Get up and stand vvv vvv among [us] So he got up [and] stood [there]

verses.original: δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἐπερωτῶ ὑμᾶς εἰ ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι σῶσαι ψυχὴν ἢ ἀπολέσαι
verses.transliteration: de ho Iēsous eipen pros autous Eperōtō hymas ei exestin tō sabbatō agathopoiēsai ē kakopoiēsai sōsai psychēn ē apolesai
verses.literal: Then - Jesus said to them I ask you which is lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil to save life or to destroy [it]

verses.original: Καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντας αὐτοὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἔκτεινον σου τὴν χεῖρά δὲ ὁ ἐποίησεν καὶ αὐτοῦ ἡ χεὶρ ἀπεκατεστάθη
verses.transliteration: Kai periblepsamenos pantas autous eipen autō Ekteinon sou tēn cheira de ho epoiēsen kai autou hē cheir apekatestathē
verses.literal: And after looking around at all of them He said to [the man] Stretch out your - hand - - He did [so] and vvv vvv [it] was restored

verses.original: δὲ αὐτοὶ ἐπλήσθησαν ἀνοίας καὶ διελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους τί ἂν ποιήσαιεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: de autoi eplēsthēsan anoias kai dielaloun pros allēlous ti an poiēsaien tō Iēsou
verses.literal: But [the scribes and Pharisees] were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what . . . they might do - to Jesus

verses.original: δὲ Ἐγένετο ἐν ταύταις ταῖς ἡμέραις αὐτὸν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι καὶ ἦν διανυκτερεύων ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: de Egeneto en tautais tais hēmerais auton exelthein eis to oros proseuxasthai kai ēn dianyktereuōn en tē proseuchē tou Theou
verses.literal: - - In those - days vvv [Jesus] went out to the mountain to pray and vvv He spent the night in - prayer - to God

verses.original: καὶ ὅτε ἡμέρα ἐγένετο προσεφώνησεν αὐτοῦ τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος δώδεκα ἀπ’ αὐτῶν οὓς καὶ ὠνόμασεν ἀποστόλους
verses.transliteration: kai hote hēmera egeneto prosephōnēsen autou tous mathētas kai eklexamenos dōdeka ap’ autōn hous kai ōnomasen apostolous
verses.literal: - When daylight came He called His - disciples {to Him} and chose twelve of them whom - He also designated as apostles

verses.original: Σίμωνα ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν Πέτρον καὶ αὐτοῦ τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἀνδρέαν καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον
verses.transliteration: Simōna hon kai ōnomasen Petron kai autou ton adelphon Andrean kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn kai Philippon kai Bartholomaion
verses.literal: Simon whom - He named Peter and his - brother Andrew - James and John - Philip and Bartholomew

verses.original: καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν καλούμενον Ζηλωτὴν
verses.transliteration: kai Maththaion kai Thōman kai Iakōbon Halphaiou kai Simōna ton kaloumenon Zēlōtēn
verses.literal: - Matthew and Thomas - James [son of] Alphaeus and Simon - called [the] Zealot

verses.original: καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριὼθ ὃς ἐγένετο προδότης
verses.transliteration: kai Ioudan Iakōbou kai Ioudan Iskariōth hos egeneto prodotēs
verses.literal: - Judas [son] of James and Judas Iscariot who became [a] traitor

verses.original: Καὶ καταβὰς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔστη ἐπὶ πεδινοῦ τόπου καὶ πολὺς ὄχλος αὐτοῦ μαθητῶν καὶ πολὺ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῆς παραλίου Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος
verses.transliteration: Kai katabas met’ autōn estē epi pedinou topou kai polys ochlos autou mathētōn kai poly plēthos tou laou apo pasēs tēs Ioudaias kai Ierousalēm kai tēs paraliou Tyrou kai Sidōnos
verses.literal: Then [Jesus] came down with them [and] stood on a level place - A large crowd of His disciples [was there] along with a great number of people from all over - Judea - Jerusalem and the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon

verses.original: οἳ ἦλθον ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰαθῆναι ἀπὸ αὐτῶν τῶν νόσων καὶ οἱ ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ ἀκαθάρτων πνευμάτων ἐθεραπεύοντο
verses.transliteration: hoi ēlthon akousai autou kai iathēnai apo autōn tōn nosōn kai hoi enochloumenoi apo akathartōn pneumatōn etherapeuonto
verses.literal: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their - diseases and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed

verses.original: καὶ ὁ πᾶς ὄχλος ἐζήτουν ἅπτεσθαι αὐτοῦ ὅτι δύναμις ἐξήρχετο παρ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰᾶτο πάντας
verses.transliteration: kai ho pas ochlos ezētoun haptesthai autou hoti dynamis exērcheto par’ autou kai iato pantas
verses.literal: - The entire crowd was trying to touch Him because power was coming from Him and healing them all

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπάρας αὐτοῦ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς εἰς αὐτοῦ τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτὸς ἔλεγεν Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοί Ὅτι ὑμετέρα ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai eparas autou tous ophthalmous eis autou tous mathētas autos elegen Makarioi hoi ptōchoi Hoti hymetera estin hē basileia tou Theou
verses.literal: - Looking up . . . . . . . . . at His - disciples [Jesus] said Blessed [are] [you] who are poor for yours is the kingdom - of God

verses.original: Μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν Ὅτι χορτασθήσεσθε Μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν Ὅτι γελάσετε
verses.transliteration: Makarioi hoi peinōntes nyn Hoti chortasthēsesthe Makarioi hoi klaiontes nyn Hoti gelasete
verses.literal: Blessed [are] [you] who hunger now for you will be filled Blessed [are] [you] who weep now for you will laugh

verses.original: Μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν οἱ ἄνθρωποι μισήσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὅταν ἀφορίσωσιν καὶ ὀνειδίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ἐκβάλωσιν ὑμῶν τὸ ὄνομα ὡς πονηρὸν ἕνεκα τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
verses.transliteration: Makarioi este hotan hoi anthrōpoi misēsōsin hymas kai hotan aphorisōsin kai oneidisōsin hymas kai ekbalōsin hymōn to onoma hōs ponēron heneka tou Huiou tou anthrōpou
verses.literal: Blessed are you when - people hate you and when they exclude [you] and insult you and reject your - name as evil because of the Son - of Man

verses.original: χάρητε ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σκιρτήσατε γὰρ ἰδοὺ πολὺς ὑμῶν ὁ μισθὸς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ γὰρ αὐτὰ οἱ πατέρες ἐποίουν τοῖς προφήταις κατὰ τὰ αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: charēte en ekeinē tē hēmera kai skirtēsate gar idou polys hymōn ho misthos en tō ouranō gar auta hoi pateres epoioun tois prophētais kata ta autōn
verses.literal: Rejoice in that - day and leap for joy because . . . great [is] your - reward in - heaven For their - fathers treated the prophets vvv vvv in the same way

verses.original: Πλὴν οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς πλουσίοις Ὅτι ἀπέχετε ὑμῶν τὴν παράκλησιν
verses.transliteration: Plēn ouai hymin tois plousiois Hoti apechete hymōn tēn paraklēsin
verses.literal: But woe to you who are rich for you have already received your - comfort

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν οἱ ἐμπεπλησμένοι νῦν Ὅτι πεινάσετε Οὐαί οἱ γελῶντες νῦν Ὅτι πενθήσετε καὶ κλαύσετε
verses.transliteration: Ouai hymin hoi empeplēsmenoi nyn Hoti peinasete Ouai hoi gelōntes nyn Hoti penthēsete kai klausete
verses.literal: Woe to you who are well fed now for you will hunger Woe to [you] who laugh now for you will mourn and weep

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὅταν πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἴπωσιν καλῶς ὑμᾶς γὰρ αὐτὰ οἱ πατέρες ἐποίουν τοῖς ψευδοπροφήταις Κατὰ τὰ αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Ouai hotan pantes hoi anthrōpoi eipōsin kalōs hymas gar auta hoi pateres epoioun tois pseudoprophētais Kata ta autōn
verses.literal: Woe to you when all - men speak well of you for their - fathers treated the false prophets vvv vvv in the same way

verses.original: Ἀλλὰ ὑμῖν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν λέγω Ἀγαπᾶτε ὑμῶν τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ποιεῖτε καλῶς τοῖς μισοῦσιν ὑμᾶς
verses.transliteration: Alla hymin tois akouousin legō Agapate hymōn tous echthrous poieite kalōs tois misousin hymas
verses.literal: But to those of you who will listen I say Love your - enemies do good to those who hate you

verses.original: εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμᾶς προσεύχεσθε περὶ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς
verses.transliteration: eulogeite tous katarōmenous hymas proseuchesthe peri tōn epēreazontōn hymas
verses.literal: bless those who curse you pray for those who mistreat you

verses.original: τύπτοντί σε ἐπὶ τὴν σιαγόνα πάρεχε τῷ τὴν ἄλλην καὶ καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντός σου τὸ ἱμάτιον μὴ κωλύσῃς τὸν χιτῶνα καὶ
verses.transliteration: typtonti se epi tēn siagona pareche tō tēn allēn kai kai apo tou airontos sou to himation mē kōlysēs ton chitōna kai
verses.literal: [If someone] strikes you on [one] cheek turn to him the other also And vvv [if someone] takes your - cloak do not withhold [your] tunic as well

verses.original: δίδου παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει
verses.transliteration: didou panti aitounti se kai apo tou airontos ta sa mē apaitei
verses.literal: Give to everyone who asks you and vvv [if anyone] takes what [is] yours {do} not demand [it] back

verses.original: καὶ ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα οἱ ἄνθρωποι ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: kai poieite autois homoiōs kathōs thelete hina hoi anthrōpoi poiōsin hymin
verses.literal: - Do to [others] - as you would have - - [them] do to you

verses.original: Καὶ εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς ποία χάρις ἐστίν ὑμῖν γὰρ καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀγαπῶσιν τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας αὐτοὺς
verses.transliteration: Kai ei agapate tous agapōntas hymas poia charis estin hymin gar kai hoi hamartōloi agapōsin tous agapōntas autous
verses.literal: - If you love those who love you what credit is that to you - Even - sinners love those who love them

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐὰν ἀγαθοποιῆτε τοὺς ἀγαθοποιοῦντας ὑμᾶς ποία χάρις ἐστίν ὑμῖν καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ποιοῦσιν τὸ αὐτὸ
verses.transliteration: kai gar ean agathopoiēte tous agathopoiountas hymas poia charis estin hymin kai hoi hamartōloi poiousin to auto
verses.literal: - - If you do good to those who do good to you what credit is that to you Even - sinners do the same

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν δανίσητε παρ’ ὧν ἐλπίζετε λαβεῖν ποία χάρις ἐστίν ὑμῖν καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ δανίζουσιν ἁμαρτωλοῖς ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν τὰ ἴσα
verses.transliteration: kai ean danisēte par’ hōn elpizete labein poia charis estin hymin kai hamartōloi danizousin hamartōlois hina apolabōsin ta isa
verses.literal: And if you lend [to those] from whom you expect repayment what credit is that to you Even sinners lend to sinners expecting to be repaid - in full

verses.original: Πλὴν ἀγαπᾶτε ὑμῶν τοὺς ἐχθροὺς καὶ ἀγαθοποιεῖτε καὶ δανίζετε ἀπελπίζοντες μηδὲν καὶ ὑμῶν ὁ μισθὸς ἔσται πολύς καὶ ἔσεσθε υἱοὶ Ὑψίστου ὅτι αὐτὸς ἐστιν χρηστός ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀχαρίστους καὶ πονηρούς
verses.transliteration: Plēn agapate hymōn tous echthrous kai agathopoieite kai danizete apelpizontes mēden kai hymōn ho misthos estai polys kai esesthe huioi Hypsistou hoti autos estin chrēstos epi tous acharistous kai ponērous
verses.literal: But love your - enemies - do good [to them] and lend [to them] expecting nothing in return . . . Then your - reward will be great and you will be sons of the Most High for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked

verses.original: Γίνεσθε οἰκτίρμονες καὶ καθὼς ὑμῶν ὁ Πατὴρ ἐστίν οἰκτίρμων
verses.transliteration: Ginesthe oiktirmones kai kathōs hymōn ho Patēr estin oiktirmōn
verses.literal: Be merciful just as your - Father is merciful

verses.original: Καὶ μὴ κρίνετε καὶ οὐ μὴ κριθῆτε καὶ μὴ καταδικάζετε καὶ οὐ μὴ καταδικασθῆτε ἀπολύετε καὶ ἀπολυθήσεσθε
verses.transliteration: Kai mē krinete kai ou mē krithēte kai mē katadikazete kai ou mē katadikasthēte apolyete kai apolythēsesthe
verses.literal: - {Do} not judge and vvv vvv you will not be judged - {Do} not condemn and vvv vvv you will not be condemned Forgive and you will be forgiven

verses.original: δίδοτε καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν καλὸν μέτρον πεπιεσμένον σεσαλευμένον ὑπερεκχυννόμενον δώσουσιν εἰς ὑμῶν τὸν κόλπον γὰρ ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε ἀντιμετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: didote kai dothēsetai hymin kalon metron pepiesmenon sesaleumenon hyperekchynnomenon dōsousin eis hymōn ton kolpon gar hō metrō metreite antimetrēthēsetai hymin
verses.literal: Give and it will be given to you A good measure pressed down shaken together [and] running over will be poured into your - lap For with the measure you [use] it will be measured back to you

verses.original: δὲ Εἶπεν καὶ αὐτοῖς παραβολὴν δύναται τυφλὸς Μήτι ὁδηγεῖν τυφλὸν οὐχὶ ἀμφότεροι ἐμπεσοῦνται εἰς βόθυνον
verses.transliteration: de Eipen kai autois parabolēn dynatai typhlos Mēti hodēgein typhlon ouchi amphoteroi empesountai eis bothynon
verses.literal: - [Jesus] also told . . . them a parable Can a blind [man] vvv lead a blind [man] {Will they} not both fall into a pit

verses.original: μαθητὴς ἔστιν οὐκ ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον δὲ πᾶς κατηρτισμένος ἔσται ὡς ὁ αὐτοῦ διδάσκαλος
verses.transliteration: mathētēs estin ouk hyper ton didaskalon de pas katērtismenos estai hōs ho autou didaskalos
verses.literal: A disciple is not above [his] teacher but everyone [who is] fully trained will be like - his teacher

verses.original: δὲ Τί βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ σου ἀδελφοῦ τοῦ ὀφθαλμῷ τὴν δὲ οὐ κατανοεῖς δοκὸν τὴν ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ ὀφθαλμῷ
verses.transliteration: de Ti blepeis to karphos to en tō sou adelphou tou ophthalmō tēn de ou katanoeis dokon tēn en tō idiō ophthalmō
verses.literal: - Why do you look at the speck - in - your brother’s - eye - but fail to notice [the] beam - in [your] own eye

verses.original: πῶς δύνασαι λέγειν τῷ σου ἀδελφῷ Ἀδελφέ ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ σου ὀφθαλμῷ αὐτὸς οὐ βλέπων δοκὸν τὴν ἐν τῷ σοῦ ὀφθαλμῷ ὑποκριτά πρῶτον ἔκβαλε τὴν δοκὸν ἐκ σοῦ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ τοῦ σου ἀδελφοῦ ὀφθαλμῷ
verses.transliteration: pōs dynasai legein tō sou adelphō Adelphe aphes ekbalō to karphos to en tō sou ophthalmō autos ou blepōn dokon tēn en tō sou ophthalmō hypokrita prōton ekbale tēn dokon ek sou tou ophthalmou kai tote diablepseis ekbalein to karphos to en tō tou sou adelphou ophthalmō
verses.literal: How can you say - - - Brother let me take the speck {out} of - your eye [while] you yourself vvv fail to see [the] beam - in - your own eye [You] hypocrite First take the beam out of your own eye and then you will see clearly to remove the speck - from - - your brother’s eye

verses.original: γάρ ἐστιν Οὐ καλὸν δένδρον ποιοῦν σαπρόν καρπὸν οὐδὲ πάλιν σαπρὸν δένδρον ποιοῦν καλόν καρπὸν
verses.transliteration: gar estin Ou kalon dendron poioun sapron karpon oude palin sapron dendron poioun kalon karpon
verses.literal: - - No good tree bears bad fruit nor [does] [a] bad tree bear good fruit

verses.original: γὰρ ἕκαστον δένδρον γινώσκεται ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου καρποῦ γὰρ οὐ σῦκα συλλέγουσιν ἐξ ἀκανθῶν οὐδὲ τρυγῶσιν σταφυλὴν ἐκ βάτου
verses.transliteration: gar hekaston dendron ginōsketai ek tou idiou karpou gar ou syka syllegousin ex akanthōn oude trygōsin staphylēn ek batou
verses.literal: For each tree is known by its own fruit Indeed vvv figs are not gathered from thornbushes nor - grapes from brambles

verses.original: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος προφέρει ἀγαθόν τὸ ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ τῆς αὐτοῦ καρδίας καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς προφέρει τὸ πονηρόν ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ γὰρ ἐκ περισσεύματος καρδίας αὐτοῦ τὸ στόμα λαλεῖ
verses.transliteration: ho agathos anthrōpos propherei agathon to ek tou agathou thēsaurou tēs autou kardias kai ho ponēros propherei to ponēron ek tou ponērou gar ek perisseumatos kardias autou to stoma lalei
verses.literal: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart and the evil [man] brings - evil [things] out of the evil [treasure of his heart] For out of the overflow of the heart - the mouth speaks

verses.original: δέ Τί καλεῖτε με Κύριε κύριε καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω
verses.transliteration: de Ti kaleite me Kyrie kyrie kai ou poieite ha legō
verses.literal: - Why do you call Me Lord Lord [but] {do} not do what I say

verses.original: ὑποδείξω ὑμῖν τίνι ἐστὶν ὅμοιος Πᾶς ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρός με καὶ ἀκούων μου τῶν λόγων καὶ ποιῶν αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: hypodeixō hymin tini estin homoios Pas ho erchomenos pros me kai akouōn mou tōn logōn kai poiōn autous
verses.literal: I will show you what he is like - who comes to Me and hears My - words and acts on them

verses.original: ἐστιν ὅμοιός ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομοῦντι οἰκίαν ὃς ἔσκαψεν καὶ ἐβάθυνεν καὶ ἔθηκεν θεμέλιον ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν δὲ πλημμύρης γενομένης ὁ ποταμὸς προσέρηξεν ἐκείνῃ τῇ οἰκίᾳ καὶ ἴσχυσεν οὐκ σαλεῦσαι αὐτὴν διὰ αὐτήν τὸ οἰκοδομῆσθαι καλῶς
verses.transliteration: estin homoios anthrōpō oikodomounti oikian hos eskapsen kai ebathynen kai ethēken themelion epi tēn petran de plēmmyrēs genomenēs ho potamos proserēxen ekeinē tē oikia kai ischysen ouk saleusai autēn dia autēn to oikodomēsthai kalōs
verses.literal: He is like a man building a house who dug down - deep and laid [his] foundation on the rock When [the] flood came the torrent crashed against that - house but could not shake it because it - was well built . . .

verses.original: δὲ ὁ ἀκούσας καὶ μὴ ποιήσας ἐστιν ὅμοιός ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομήσαντι οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν χωρὶς θεμελίου ὁ ποταμός προσέρηξεν ᾗ καὶ εὐθὺς συνέπεσεν καὶ μέγα ἐγένετο τὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἐκείνης ῥῆγμα
verses.transliteration: de ho akousas kai mē poiēsas estin homoios anthrōpō oikodomēsanti oikian epi tēn gēn chōris themeliou ho potamos proserēxen hē kai euthys synepesen kai mega egeneto to tēs oikias ekeinēs rhēgma
verses.literal: But the [one who] hears [My words] and {does} not act on them is like a man who built [his] house on - ground without [a] foundation The torrent crashed against [that house] and immediately it fell and great was vvv vvv vvv [its] destruction
